text: A month of growth, collaboration, and reflection — 940 contribution tokens, 36 new members, and the beginning of the next chapter for The Guild.
October has been an exciting month for The Guild — the peer-run network where developers build reputation through real contributions, peer attestations, and open collaboration.
Our community kept growing, shipping code, and shaping what on-chain reputation can look like in practice.
4 contributors active this month. 34 tickets closed. 26 tags (potential future Guild badges). 940 contribution tokens to be distributed. 36 new members joined Discord.
That’s strong activity for a young open-source community — and it shows how much energy there is around building in the open.
This month, The Guild was listed on OnlyDust, a platform connecting open-source projects with contributors. Combined with Hacktoberfest, this brought a wave of new developers eager to collaborate.
It’s been great to see people not only coding, but also reviewing and learning from each other — which is exactly the spirit of The Guild.
These contributions created the perfect foundation for distributing the first Guild Attestations on EAS, turning real work into verifiable, on-chain reputation.
While we successfully onboarded many new contributors, most were junior engineers, creating a bottleneck in reviews. We now need more senior mentors to maintain code quality and support learning.

We also saw little peer-to-peer badge activity. Very few members gave badges to others, showing that attestations are still too centralized. We’ll focus on onboarding mentors and encouraging horizontal recognition.
Some features block others, so we’ll work on identifying parallelizable tasks to keep contribution momentum high.
Looking ahead, our next priorities are clear.
Recruit senior mentors and reviewers to support contributor growth.
Design and build new features like a project board and automated workflows for the Guild.
Expand EAS attestations, rewarding members for real, peer-verified activity.
The next phase will involve AI — tools to help developers collaborate, attest, and learn more intelligently.
Every contribution, review, and badge strengthens the network and brings us closer to a future where developers build trust through verifiable collaboration, not credentials.
